title: Mount snowboard bindings for a 40 cm duck stance and screw them down
instruction: Mount this rental snowboard's bindings for a 40 cm duck stance centred on the red cross, heels on the edge nearest you, and screw both down.
context: Before a rental snowboard goes out, a technician mounts its bindings to the rider's stance: the width from the shop chart (40 cm for this child) centred on the reference mark, the discs set for a beginner's duck stance, each disc screwed through its slots into the board's threaded inserts. A misplaced or loose binding comes off. Hardest physical part: carry a 0.35 kg binding by its 10 mm highback and set it flat, angle within 3 degrees, each 10 mm slot within 4 mm of an 8 mm insert across the slot; then hold each screw by its 12 mm head, feed its 5 mm shank through a slot into the insert and turn it a full turn in regrips without lifting its washer 3 mm. Aligning a slotted part over a threaded-insert pattern and screwing it down is regular work of team assemblers (O*NET 51-2092.00) and general maintenance and repair workers (49-9071.00), each well over 500,000 US workers; ski-shop rental clerks (41-2021.00) do it as here.
setup: Bimanual YAM station, real size; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; the arm bases are at y +30.5 and -30.5 cm. All parts are fixed except the two bindings and the eight screws. (1) Board: a child's snowboard top as a flat rigid plank 1100 mm long along y (nose at y +55 cm, tail at -55 cm), 240 mm wide (x 18 to 42 cm, heel edge toward the robot) and 10 mm thick, white with a 4 mm black centre line at x 30 cm. Sixteen M6 inserts on the 4 x 4 pattern: square bores 8 mm across and 9 mm deep with dark floors (no thread: see fidelity), in two rows across the board at x 28 and 32 cm, at y +14, +18, +22 and +26 cm on the nose half and -14, -18, -22 and -26 cm on the tail half (40 mm apart). (2) A red tape cross, two 30 x 4 x 0.5 mm strips, at x 30 cm, y 0. (3) Two child's bindings, rigid plastic, about 0.35 kg each (a real one's ribbed, hollow plates weigh less than solid plates of these outer sizes): a black baseplate 230 mm heel to toe and 130 mm wide with an 8 mm floor, sidewalls 6 mm thick and 40 mm tall, and a highback 10 mm thick, 130 mm wide and 100 mm tall across its heel end; set flush in the floor, a grey 4 x 4 disc 88 mm across with four slots, each 10 mm wide and 24 mm long, centred on a 40 mm square with their long sides square to the disc. The discs are preset and fixed in their baseplates: the nose binding's baseplate is turned 15 degrees counter-clockwise (seen from above) from its disc's slot square, the tail binding's 15 degrees clockwise. (4) Eight M6 binding screws, steel, 6 g each (a real one with its washer is about 8 to 10 g): a round head 12 mm across and 5 mm tall on an 18 mm washer 1.5 mm thick, and a 5 mm shank (the thread's core) reaching 14.5 mm below the washer. Four stand head up, washers resting on the holder's top, in each of two fixed blue holders (30 x 120 x 24 mm, 6 mm sockets 20 mm deep) on the table beyond the board's toe edge at x 45.5 cm: at y +21.5, +24.5, +27.5 and +30.5 cm, and at the same negative y. Start: both bindings lie flat on the board's ends, disc centres on the centre line, toes toward the ends and 5 mm from them: the nose binding's disc at y +43 cm, the tail binding's at -43 cm. A binding's angle is the direction from heel to toe seen from above, in degrees from +x (straight across the board, away from the robot), positive toward the nose: +90 for the nose binding at the start, -90 for the tail binding. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Rules during the trial: a screw is engaged once its shank has gone through a slot of a binding into an insert (tip 5 mm or more down it), upright within 10 degrees, washer within 1 mm of the disc's top. While engaged its turn about its axis is summed (clockwise seen from above up, counter-clockwise down); once the washer is 3 mm up, the shank leaves that slot or insert, or it tilts past 10 degrees, it disengages and the sum resets to 0. At 360 degrees the screw is driven: held from then on upright where it stands. A flat binding whose four slots hold driven screws is clamped: held from then on where it lies. Neither is undone. End state, per binding: aligned: flat (underside's centre within 1.5 mm of the board's top, tilted 3 degrees or less), angle within 3 degrees of its target, each slot over an insert (the insert's centre within 11.0 mm of the slot's centre along the slot and 4.0 mm across it); seated n: n slots hold a screw 5 mm or more down an insert, upright within 5 degrees, washer within 1 mm of the disc's top; fastened: aligned, clamped, four driven screws. Targets: the binding nearer the nose +15 degrees (toe toward the nose), the other -15. Every score above 0 needs, on every step of the last 1 s, both grippers released (each finger zone, defined in the README, 30 mm or more from every binding and screw; an unreadable gripper or a distance that cannot be computed is not released) and every binding and screw moved 2 mm or less and turned 1 degree or less. Scores: 1.0 both fastened on the middle squares (inserts at |y| 18 and 22 cm: discs 400 mm apart, centred on the cross). 0.75 both fastened on other squares (discs 320 to 480 mm apart). 0.5 both aligned with four screws seated in each, not both fastened. 0.25 exactly one aligned with four screws seated. 0 anything else (wrong angle, heel forward, presets swapped, three screws, a screw in an insert with no slot over it, a part held, touched or moving). 0 for the rest of the trial once a binding or a screw falls off the table (20 mm or more below its top). The trial ends once 1.0 has held for 1 s; otherwise the score is the end state at the run limit. In a real trial, with threaded inserts: slots over inserts by eye; a screw seated when threaded in until a 1 mm feeler gauge no longer passes under its washer, and driven by the next full turn (M6 pitch 1.0 mm), which brings the washer down on the disc, counted by a paint witness mark on its head; a binding clamped when it cannot be slid by hand; its angle with a protractor against the board's centre line; the stance with a tape.
fidelity: Real size. Friction 1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic. Simplified: smooth 8 mm square bores, 5 mm shanks, no threads: a screw slides down to its seat (a real one threads in 6.5 turns) and one clockwise turn while seated counts as driven; the screw is then welded upright, and a binding with four driven screws welded flat (pose rewrites). Slots: 2.5 mm play a side (real: close) for the arm's placement error. Highback 100 mm, lower than real, to keep its grip in reach. Flat fixed board; no straps.
reset_notes: Take out any driven screws and put all eight back in their holders, head up. Put each binding back on its parked spot on its own end of the board: disc on the centre line, toe toward that end and 5 mm from it. The board, the cross and the holders are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
